region.name: Leadership People Profiles
region.summary: Profiles and working notes on key people around the author (engineers, product and bank partners, cofounder Aleks, and VP Engineering finalists), covering ownership areas, burnout and comp concerns, the Series B timeline, and the pending VP Eng decision.

brief.text:
This region holds the author's working profiles of the people who matter most during the Series B push: direct reports, product and sponsor-bank partners, cofounder Aleks, and the two VP Engineering finalists. Marcus Bell (Payments lead) has been overloaded since August and is the top people risk; the mitigation plan is to remove load now by moving the Pillar sync to Sarah and the ADR-032 build to Devon, give him a week off after GA, make his comp adjustment first after close, and reassure him that the August sweep job decision was shared. The VP Eng hire is partly intended to relieve him. Devon Park, senior backend engineer reporting to Marcus (skip-level held), owns the ACH outbox worker, DriveWealth position reconciliation and alerting, and deletion of the old Sidekiq ACH code, and wants to lead ADR-032. His track record includes catching the April 6 anomaly, building the shadow-mode diff harness for ADR-024, a reconciliation job that caught the Sep 26 double-debits in 47 minutes, and surfacing the Sep 15 position drift. Nadia Okafor, iOS tech lead on a manager-track trial with first report Theo Brandt, owns the SwiftUI + TCA refactor and iOS hiring. She has now twice been told her comp review will come 'post-Series B', which is tracked as an open risk. The senior iOS offer to Ama is stalled because band pay is below market and the offer-accept rate is 55%. Renee Alvarez, Head of Product, is handling investing GA (at risk after a no-go), Android parity, and card issuing slipping to Q1 2027, and is on a CPO candidacy path.

External and leadership relationships carry the timeline. Aleks needs a Series B close by Nov 14, a clean data room by Oct 12, tech diligence on Oct 14, the board meeting on Oct 21, and the VP Eng decision by Oct 20. He also needs Renee raised as a CPO candidate, aligned messaging to Kavi, no surprises in the board deck, and the truth about GA. The author has not yet told Aleks about their own exhaustion. Karim Haddad is the account lead at sponsor bank Pillar Bank, with team contacts Theresa Lowe, Priya Shah, and Brent Ochoa. The relationship timeline runs from the June ACH cut-over coordination through the Sep 26 incident to the Oct 2 QBR, where Pillar requested a written remediation plan and the investing funding cap was discussed. A separate high-severity compliance item, owned by Sam Whitfield, warns that the late Q3 access review could become a SOC 2 Type II exception and remains an open todo.

The pending VP Eng decision is between Tomas Reyes (ex-Brex) and Grace Liu. Reyes is stronger on money-movement operations, sponsor-bank relationships, incident command, and tech diligence. He is weaker on growing managers, and his process-heavy style risks disengaging a light-process, high-trust, ceremony-averse team. The author is weighing whether his rigor is warranted after two incidents or would be an overcorrection. Typical questions for this region include: who owns a given payments or iOS system, how to relieve Marcus, what has been promised on comp and to whom, key Series B and diligence dates, the status of the Pillar Bank relationship and remediation plan, the tradeoffs between Reyes and Liu, and the open risks with their owners.
